newsitem.title: INDIA: Low-caste leader Narayanan elected India president.
newsitem.headline: Low-caste leader Narayanan elected India president.

text.p: Vice-President Kocheril Raman Narayanan was elected India's 10th president on Thursday, an Election Commission spokesman said.

Narayanan, the first member of a low Hindu caste to be voted president of the world's biggest democracy, was backed by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front coalition, the Congress party and the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.

Narayanan was elected by an electoral college comprising 4,848 legislators of the federal parliament and state legislatures, who voted in a secret nationwide ballot through a system of proportional representation.
The 76-year-old former diplomat, who was born in a poor family, won 4,231 votes. His rival, former chief election commissioner T.N. Seshan, polled 240 votes, the Election Commission spokesman said.
Narayanan is scheduled to take office for a five-year term on July 25, three weeks before the 50th anniversary of India's independence from Britain on August 15.

Traditionally a largely ceremonial job, the post of the president has been seen as crucial following the emergence of coalition politics in which the head of state can play a key role in the formation of governments.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma's five-year term expires on July 25. Although eligible for a second term, Sharma did not seek re-election.
